# Authentication
There are two modes of authentication:
* By token: after identification with your login credentials
* By cookie: by reusing a valid session ID

get.description: Returns the paginated list of Business Activities the user is allowed to see. Admins and users with the all_business_views grant see every BA; other users only see the BAs reachable through their business views. Searchable / sortable fields: id, name, description, is_enabled.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Filter by field and operator, e.g. ?name[lk]=foo, ?id[eq]=1, ?is_enabled[eq]=true. Allowed operators: eq, neq, lk, nlk, in, nin.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort by field and direction, e.g. ?sort[name]=ASC.

parameters.name: show_only_top_level
parameters.description: When true, only top-level Business Activities (roots and orphans) are returned; BAs referenced as a child of another (accessible) BA are hidden. Absent or false keeps every accessible BA.

parameters.name: itemsPerPage
parameters.description: The number of items per page. Values above 100 are capped to 100. Defaults to the "Limit per page" platform setting, or to 30 when it is not set or invalid.

422.description: Invalid parameters (window larger than 30 days, start >= end, end provided without start, end in the future, or a non-integer start/end)

500.description: The reporting history contains an event that cannot be processed (server-side data corruption)

get.summary: Get the status timeline of a Business Activity
get.description: Returns the contiguous status bands of a Business Activity over a time window, read from the reporting history (mod_bam_reporting_ba_events, populated by the Broker BAM reporting output; without it the collection is empty) and clipped to the window. A band reopens on every change of status, downtime or level, so several bands may share the same status. The ongoing band has `end: null` and `is_ongoing: true`, but its `duration` is still returned, measured from the band start to the window end. Timestamps are Unix seconds. By default the window covers the last 24 hours; `start`/`end` are optional and the window is capped at 30 days. An `end` in the future is rejected with a 422. The response is not paginated.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Window start, Unix seconds. Optional. When omitted with no `end`, the last 24 hours are returned. When provided alone, `end` defaults to now.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Window end, Unix seconds. Optional, but requires `start`; providing `end` alone is rejected. Must satisfy start < end, end - start <= 30 days, and end <= now (a future end is rejected).

403.description: Access denied to this Business Activity

500.description: The Business Activity tree carries an unsupported legacy value that cannot be processed (server-side data corruption)

get.summary: Get the full tree of a Business Activity
get.description:
Returns the complete recursive tree structure of a BA with all its indicators. BA children outside the user's ACL scope are visible (name + impact) but not expandable; they carry `acl_restricted: true` on the indicator node so the front can render them greyed and forbid editing. In-scope BA nodes carry `acl_restricted: false`. The field is absent for non-Business-Activity indicators.

**Supersedes a legacy path.** This endpoint replaces `/api/latest/configuration/business-activities/{id}/tree`, which stays reachable for cloud clients released before the `bam/` migration but is **deprecated and scheduled for removal**. That legacy path is intentionally omitted from this documentation; new integrations must use the `/bam/...` path described here.

400.description: Malformed request rejected before domain validation — a `BadRequestHttpException`. On the canonical `/api/bam` path this covers the non-`ValidationException` cases only: calculation-method threshold coherence (e.g. warning above critical, percentage above 100) and camelCase keys instead of snake_case. Payload schema / constraint violations return `422` here (see below); they are downgraded to `400` only on the deprecated `/api/latest` alias.

403.description: Access denied to this Business Activity

example.message: You are not allowed to update this Business Activity tree
Adding Business Activity #42 as an indicator of #7 would create a cyclic dependency.

422.description: Validation rejection. Two sources, both `422` on `/api/bam`: payload schema / constraint violations on the input DTOs (`ValidationException` — wrong indicator type, missing required field such as `parent_resource_id`, `calculation_method.value` shape, unknown impact id), and business-rule violations needing database context (`UnprocessableEntityHttpException` from `UpdateTreeInputValidator` — BA does not exist, is not part of the current tree, name already used by another BA, referenced resource/host does not resolve). On the deprecated `/api/latest` alias the `ValidationException` subset is downgraded to `400`.

example.message: [business_activities[0].name] Business Activity name "Foo" is already used.

500.description: The Business Activity tree carries an unsupported legacy value that cannot be processed (server-side data corruption)

patch.description:
Partially updates a Business Activity tree. All sections (`business_activities`, `indicators_added`, `indicators_updated`, `indicators_removed`) are optional. Mutations targeting Business Activities outside the user's ACL scope are silently ignored (no info leak on the existence of unauthorised resources). The companion GET `acl_restricted: true` flag tells the front which BA nodes to filter out of the payload client-side; the back-side silent-drop remains as defense-in-depth.

**Indicator references — kpi_id or uuid:** entries in `indicators_removed` and the `id` field of `indicators_updated` accept either the kpi_id (positive integer) or the uuid string from `GET /tree` (`<shortType><resourceId>`, optionally prefixed with `h<host>-` for host-scoped types). The uuid form is stable across the legacy `centreon_business_activity` PUT that drops and re-inserts kpi rows on every save — clients that may interleave that PUT with this PATCH should reference indicators by uuid to avoid stale kpi_id lookups. A single uuid resolves to every kpi_id matching it (duplicate-link case), so the action applies to every matching row.

**Silent-drop on unknown indicator references:** by design, an `id` in `indicators_updated` or `indicators_removed` that does not resolve to anything in the loaded tree — truly unknown, stale kpi_id, unknown uuid, or belonging to a tree the user cannot access — is dropped without error. The endpoint still returns 204. This extends the ACL anti-probing policy to indicator identity: response codes must not reveal whether an unknown id corresponds to a real resource. Clients relying on feedback about their own mistakes (typoed field names, stale ids) must validate client-side.

**Validation errors — 400 vs 422:** on the canonical `/api/bam` path, both payload validation (`ValidationException` on the input DTOs) and business-rule violations (`UnprocessableEntityHttpException`) return `422`; only requests rejected earlier (`BadRequestHttpException` — threshold coherence, camelCase keys) return `400`. The deprecated `/api/latest` alias keeps the previously released contract: the `ValidationException` subset is downgraded to `400` by the core `LegacyValidationStatusListener` for backward compatibility.

**Supersedes a legacy path.** This endpoint replaces `/api/latest/configuration/business-activities/{id}/tree`, which stays reachable for cloud clients released before the `bam/` migration but is **deprecated and scheduled for removal**. That legacy path is intentionally omitted from this documentation; new integrations must use the `/bam/...` path described here.

get.summary: List the KPI states of a Business Activity
get.description: Returns the first-level KPIs of a Business Activity with their state, either now or at a past instant (`at`), one member per KPI, sorted by `since` (the start of the active state: a change of status, downtime or impact), most recent first. The state is read from the reporting history: at an instant, each KPI is in the state of its event active at that instant, however old. The instant may not be older than 31 days. Without `at`, only the KPIs currently configured and enabled are listed. With `at`, a KPI deleted or disabled since (absent from the BAM reporting dimension) is still listed when the reporting links one of its events to a Business Activity event that started at or before `at` and ended within the last 31 days or is still running; its `name` is then unknown (null), and its `type` too once it is deleted from the configuration. A configured KPI with no reporting event yet is not listed. The check output and the current attempt come from the latest service alert at the instant, kept only when its status is the KPI status; with `at`, else the first alert of that status logged after `at` and at most 5 minutes after the state start. The output therefore always matches the status; when no such alert is found (e.g. purged logs), `output.available` is false. The labels and the configured impacts are those of the configuration applied at the last reload (a saved but not yet applied change is not reflected); for a KPI absent from the BAM reporting dimension, the type and impacts come from the saved configuration. The maximum check attempts are those of the monitored resource as last known; `attempt` is null for a business-activity or boolean-rule KPI, or when the type is unknown. Timestamps are Unix seconds.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: Instant of the KPI states, Unix seconds. Optional: the current states are returned when omitted. Must satisfy now - 31 days <= at <= now.

parameters.name: itemsPerPage
parameters.description: The number of items per page. Values above 100 are capped to 100. Defaults to the "Limit per page" platform setting, or to 30 when it is not set or invalid.

Token.description:
The use of the API requires a security token.

To retrieve it, you will need to authenticate yourself with your login credentials.

The token will be deleted if it has not been used for more than one hour.
Token.name: X-AUTH-TOKEN

uuid.description: Home-made identifier consumed by the front to key tree nodes (e.g. `h7-s42`, `ba12`). Not an RFC UUID.

type.description: Service | MetaService | Business Activity | Boolean Rule | Anomaly Detection

parent_resource_id.description: Present only for types Service and Anomaly Detection

calculation_method.description: Present only when type = Business Activity

icon.description:
Icon configured on the monitored resource. Present for types Service,
Anomaly Detection, and Business Activity; `null` when absent or not
applicable to the kpi type.

downtime_inheritance_mode.description: Downtime inheritance mode of the child BA (mod_bam.inherit_kpi_downtimes).

indicators.description: Present only when type = Business Activity; empty [] when BA is outside ACL scope

acl_restricted.description:
Set only when type = Business Activity. `true` when the child BA is
outside the user's ACL perimeter — the front renders the node greyed,
non-expandable, non-editable, and must not include it in
`indicators_removed` on a subsequent PATCH. `false` when the BA is in
scope. `null` (absent) for non-BA indicators and for BA nodes the
builder could not classify (missing-from-tree path).

downtime_inheritance_mode.description:
How planned downtime on this BA's KPIs influences it
(mod_bam.inherit_kpi_downtimes). null = field not modified by this PATCH.

id.description: 0 = Impact, 1 = Best Status, 2 = Worst Status, 3 = Ratio percentage, 4 = Ratio number

warning_threshold.description:
Warning-level threshold (mod_bam.level_w). Required for Ratio; must not be
sent for Best Status and Worst Status. On the same method, kept from storage
when omitted; on a method change, the stored value is not carried over.

critical_threshold.description:
Critical-level threshold (mod_bam.level_c). Optional; must not be sent for
Best Status and Worst Status. On the same method, kept from storage when
omitted; on a method change, the stored value is not carried over.

id.description:
Either a kpi_id (positive integer) or a uuid (non-empty string of
the form `<shortType><resourceId>` or `h<host>-<shortType><resourceId>`).

level_critical.description: Critical threshold (null when the calculation method has none)

BusinessActivity.jsonld.description:
Paginated Business Activities configuration listing. It lives at the same
path as the removed legacy listing endpoint
(/bam/configuration/business-activities), so it replaces it seamlessly.
Search and sort accept the legacy fields: id, name, description, is_enabled.
Pagination uses the shared page / itemsPerPage parameters; the response is the
standard Hydra collection (member / totalItems).

One status band of a Business Activity timeline. The GetCollection is

(mod_bam_reporting_ba_events, subject to the configured reporting retention)
instead of the RRD graph status. It
cohabits with the legacy /api/latest/.../timeline endpoint, kept until the
front is migrated off it. The window defaults to the last 24 h and is capped
at 30 days; the series is not paginated.

Events to notifiy as a bit flag.
